classification.difficultyReason: Sketch familiar normal curves by holding the centre or spread fixed and changing the other feature.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the same mean but different standard deviations

answer.short: Sample sketch: two bell-shaped curves with the same centre, one narrower and taller than the other.
answer.worked: Draw both curves symmetric about the same mean. Give them different spreads: the curve with the smaller standard deviation is narrower and taller.

spec.description: Authored sample solution with a common horizontal axis and common dashed mean guide; solid and dashed curves distinguish the two distributions.
spec.mathematics: Two normal density curves have the same mean and different standard deviations. Heights are inversely proportional to their standard deviations, so both curves have equal total area.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student question retains a blank drawing region.

children.label: b
children.prompt: different means but the same standard deviation.

answer.short: Sample sketch: two equally wide and equally tall bell-shaped curves with different centres.
answer.worked: Draw two normal curves with the same shape and spread. Shift one horizontally so that their centres, and therefore their means, are different.

spec.description: Authored sample solution with two horizontally translated normal curves on one axis. Solid and dashed strokes distinguish the distributions.
spec.mathematics: The curves have identical standard deviations and peak heights but different means, marked by separate dashed vertical guides.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student question retains a blank drawing region.
